content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation on § 21 (LOL-CAP), preferred-level cure.**

The section's architecture was already good — mutual cap, mutual damages exclusion, and a full set of Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), all mapped as already met.

The material failure was the cap *basis*: "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee only — a one-time USD 12,000 charge under the first Order Form — so the "twelve months" cap was illusory and well below the six-months'-fees walk-away line. The same narrow noun also gutted the payment carve-out in § 21.3.

Two surgical replacements: (1) cap becomes the greater of twelve months' lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000, keeping the existing "event giving rise to the claim" anchor and the mutuality sentence verbatim; (2) "undisputed Fees" becomes "undisputed amounts due" so all Customer payment obligations sit outside damages.
